{{Short description|none}} {{Use dmy dates|date=April 2022}} {{Infobox Hurling All-Ireland | year = 1970 | image = | dates = 3 May – 6 September 1970 | teams = 14 | connacht = | munster = Cork | leinster = Wexford | ulster = | matches = 14 | poty = [[File:Colours of Cork.svg|20px|border]] [[Pat McDonnell]] | team = Cork | titles = 21st | captain = [[Paddy Barry (St. Vincent's)|Paddy Barry]] | manager = | team2 = Wexford | captain2 = [[Michael Collins (hurler)|Michael Collins]] | manager2 = | totalgoals = 71 (5.07 per game) | totalpoints = 312 (22.28 per game) | topscorer = [[File:Colours of Cork.svg|20px|border]] [[Charlie McCarthy (hurler)|Charlie McCarthy]] (1–23) | previous = [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship 1969|1969]] | next = [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship 1971|1971]] }} The '''1970 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship''' was the 84th staging of the [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]], the [[Gaelic Athletic Association]]'s premier [[inter county|inter-county]] [[hurling]] tournament. The championship began on 3 May 1970 and ended on 6 September 1970. [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] were the [[1969 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|defending champions]] but were defeated by [[Wexford GAA|Wexford]] in the Leinster final. [[Kildare GAA|Kildare]], who won the [[All-Ireland Intermediate Hurling Championship]] in 1969, were promoted to the senior championship after a long absence. [[New York GAA|New York]] sought entry to the All-Ireland series but their request was denied. [[Galway GAA|Galway]] left the Munster Championship after ten years of participation and reverted to the old system whereby they enter the championship at the All-Ireland semi-final stage. The [[#All-Ireland final|All-Ireland final]] was played at [[Croke Park]] in [[Dublin]] on 6 September 1970 between [[Cork GAA|Cork]] and [[Wexford GAA|Wexford]], in what was their fourth meeting in the All-Ireland final overall and a first meeting in [[1956 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|14 years]]. Cork won the match by 6–21 to 5–10 to claim their 21st All-Ireland title overall and a first title in [[1966 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|four years]].{{cite news|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-30994055.html|title=Plenty of discoveries to be made in deep dive of GAA digital archive|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=15 April 2020|accessdate=14 May 2023|first=John|last=Fogarty}}{{cite news|url=https://www.echolive.ie/corksport/arid-40252727.html|title=Reeling on the banks of the Lee: History of Cork sports 1970 to 1974|publisher=Echo Live|date=31 March 2021|accessdate=14 May 2023|first=Derek|last=Daly}}{{cite news|url=https://www.irishpost.com/sport/clash-of-the-ash-the-greatest-hurlers-of-the-1970s-200485|title=CLASH OF THE ASH: The greatest hurlers of the 1970s|publisher=The Irish Post|date=2 January 2021|accessdate=14 May 2023|first=Henry|last=Wymbs}} Cork's [[Charlie McCarthy (hurler)|Charlie McCarthy]] was the championship's [[#Top scorers|top scorer]] with 1–23. Cork's [[Pat McDonnell]] was the choice for [[Texaco Hurler of the Year]].{{cite news|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport-columnists/arid-20397962.html|title=Is the full-forward role now a thing of the past?|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=6 May 2016|accessdate=19 May 2023|first=Dónal|last=O'Grady}}{{cite news|url=https://www.echolive.ie/corksport/arid-40257899.html|title=Cork hurlers and the All-Stars clocked up the miles on US tour in 1977|publisher=Echo Live|date=4 April 2021|accessdate=19 May 2023|first=Plunkett|last=Carter}} ==Rule change== As a result of a decision taken at the [[Gaelic Athletic Association]]'s (GAA) annual congress the previous year, as of 1970 all provincial finals, All-Ireland semi-finals and the All-Ireland final itself were extended to 80 minutes playing time. Prior to this all championship matches were sixty minutes in duration.{{cite news|url=https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/gaelic-games/playing-with-time-when-gaelic-games-lasted-80-minutes-1.4311122|title=Playing with time: When Gaelic games lasted 80 minutes|publisher=Irish Times|date=23 July 2020|accessdate=19 May 2023|first=Seán|last=Moran}} Lasted until 1974. ==Teams== A total of fourteen teams contested the championship, including thirteen teams from the [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship 1969|1969 championship]] and one new entrant. The [[Leinster Senior Hurling Championship|Leinster championship]] was extended to seven teams as [[Kildare GAA|Kildare]] entered the provincial series of games. They had won the [[All-Ireland Intermediate Hurling Championship|All-Ireland]] title at intermediate level in 1969 and decided to make the step up to the senior grade. [[Galway GAA|Galway]] left the [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster championship]] where they had been playing since the [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship 1959|1959 championship]] and returned to the old system whereby they entered the All-Ireland semi-finals.{{Cite web |last=Nolan |first=Pat |date=2018-05-09 |title=How GAA Championships have evolved in the last 131 years
